mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tighter monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, which may indicate broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by 0.2pp and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% in one month
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates reduced demand in the housing market, which may signal broader economic weakness and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by 5% in one month
failure_condition: If HOUST decreases by 5% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger supply-side activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases and the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real disposable personal income (RSAFS) indicates increased consumer spending power, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by 0.5% in one month
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases by 0.5% and the S&P 500 still produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS grows and the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above its 12-month moving average, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above its 12-month moving average and the S&P 500 still produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.
